race_context: East Allen County Schools (EACS), headquartered in New Haven, serves eastern Allen County through five attendance areas; average enrollment on last year's count days was nearly 9,900 students {jg_budget26}{jg_facilities}.
The board has seven members, each tied to a numbered district with an R or E designation (for example, District 1R, 2E, 3E and 4E) {jg_preview22}{jg_vacancy}.
Three seats are on the 2026 ballot, one member each: Districts 1R, 2E and 3E {jg_filing}{in_list}.

All three incumbents are running: board President Tim Hines (District 1R) and Pamela Dukes (District 3E) are unopposed; first-term incumbent Beth Wood (District 2E) is challenged by Joni Price, the only contested EACS race {jg_d2e}.

2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could declare a party; Hines, Dukes and Price filed as Republicans, and Wood did not state an affiliation (the state list shows her as Nonpartisan) {jg_d2e}{in_list}.

Budget and SEA 1 (September 2026): the proposed 2027 budget is about $157 million at a flat tax rate of 99.99 cents per $100 of assessed value; the CFO estimated tax-cap losses of about $4.7 million next year, up from $3.8 million this year and under $1 million as recently as 2024, and said the state's property tax law, SEA 1, is contributing; he said rate increases could follow in later years {jg_budget26}.

Budget tightening (September 2025): facing an estimated $4.2 million tax-cap loss, the district cut its proposed operations fund by $3.8 million and its education fund by $2 million, which the CFO said was the first decrease in allocations during his tenure {jg_budget25}.

Facilities: in July 2024 the board supported $190 million in projects, including Paul Harding Junior High/East Allen University renovations, Leo Junior-Senior High athletic upgrades, a new Southwick Elementary and a new Leo Intermediate School, financed with bonds within existing tax caps rather than a referendum; about $120 million in further needs is to be addressed later {jg_facilities}. The Leo fieldhouse, the first of the four projects to open, was dedicated in October 2026 {jg_fieldhouse}.

Board vacancy: Vice President Steve Screeton announced in June 2026 he would resign because of a move; the board took applications for his District 4E (New Haven) seat, with the appointee to serve through 2028 {jg_vacancy}.
No 2026 candidate forum was found. The Journal Gazette sent a questionnaire to the District 2E candidates; Price answered and Wood did not {jg_d2e}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board president seeking a fourth term (he won his third in 2022); unopposed and filed as a Republican {jg_preview22}{jg_d2e}.
background: Retired owner of T.E. Hines, a concrete construction company he ran for 32 years (as of 2022) {jg_preview22}.
Ball State University graduate; has served on the East Allen Career Center advisory board and been involved in youth sports {jg_preview22}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican for District 1R; unopposed {jg_filing}{jg_d2e}{in_list}.
Won a third term in 2022 against challenger George Nicklow {jg_preview22}.

items: In 2022 said he wanted the East Allen Career Center's skilled-trades programs to continue and expand {jg_preview22}.
In 2022 said an existing committee of librarians, educators and parents decides what is appropriate in school libraries {jg_preview22}.
In 2024 said the building work was overdue, noting the pandemic had stalled improvements after the New Haven construction projects {jg_facilities}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and board president.
At the October 2026 fieldhouse dedication, described the facility as teaching students teamwork, discipline and confidence {jg_fieldhouse}.
endorsements_finance: In 2022 he said he did not seek endorsements but was endorsed by the Indiana State Teachers Association and the East Allen Education Association {jg_preview22}. No endorsements or campaign finance reports for 2026 were found in local coverage.
